subject.title: gateway install/status hardcodes ~/Library/LaunchAgents — prevents boot-without-login on macOS

question: Should OpenClaw add first-class macOS system LaunchDaemon install/status support for the gateway, and what privilege, user, and environment contract should it use?
rationale: The implementation would mutate root-owned launchd service state and decide sudo UX, service user identity, durable environment handling, and coexistence with user LaunchAgents, which automation should not choose alone.

options.title: Explicit system scope with safe default
options.body: Keep user LaunchAgent as the default, add explicit system-scope install/status only with audited UserName, TMPDIR, sudo guidance, doctor/docs/tests, and no silent elevation.

options.title: Diagnostic guidance only
options.body: Do not manage LaunchDaemons yet; improve status and doctor to identify system services and provide copy-paste manual launchctl guidance.

options.title: Full LaunchDaemon lifecycle
options.body: Add install/status/start/stop/restart/uninstall support for LaunchDaemons as a larger privileged-service feature after owner review.

recommendation.title: Explicit system scope with safe default
recommendation.body: Keep user LaunchAgent as the default, add explicit system-scope install/status only with audited UserName, TMPDIR, sudo guidance, doctor/docs/tests, and no silent elevation.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest feature-history signal for the gateway service lifecycle and service adapter boundary.
